text:
maya: FYI: noticed a sharp increase in 5xx from hosted inference since ~09:42 UTC. 5xx rate ~8% on /v1/generate (baseline ~0.1%). Ticket from customer ACME-Prod just came in. Canary rollout earlier this morning flipped a new flag 'enable_trace_payload' at 09:34. Suspect relation to deploy/canary.

leo: oncall here. tagging @jordan @maya. Can you paste the deploy id / canary percentage? Any obvious logs?

jordan: I kicked the canary for rtc/rls-service at 09:33:45 with deploy id d-20260315-87. Target canary 10% initially. The flag was behind a runtime config flag we pushed (enable_trace_payload=true). It injects a base64 trace blob into the response header x-rw-trace.

maya: deploy-bot shows: 
deploy-bot: deploy d-20260315-87 -> canary 10% at 2026-03-15T09:34:10Z

samir: customer provided sample curl and response: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" 
  -H "Accept: application/json" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< content-type: application/json
< x-request-id: 6b7f2c
< {\"error\": \"gateway error\"}
```

maya: I pulled gateway logs around 09:41-09:44 and see repeated upstream errors that look like nginx/envoy header size rejections: 
```
[error] 1234#0: *567 upstream sent too big header while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.2.3.4, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.20.30.40:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai"
```
jordan: ohhh. the flag appends the trace as a header in some cases > 8KB (we base64 the trace spans). That could exceed default proxy header limits and trigger 502s from nginx. We didn't expect it to be that large for long prompts.

leo: mitigation: pause canary / scale down canary weight and rollback the flag. @deploy-bot can you pause/rollback?

deploy-bot: Received request: pause-canary d-20260315-87. Executing: set canary weight -> 0%...

deploy-bot: Canary paused. Initiating rollback of runtime flag 'enable_trace_payload' for d-20260315-87. Rollback started.

jordan: I also pushed a quick patch to not emit header if encoded length > 2000 bytes. Patch id p-339 and will require a real rollout, but we can roll that after rollback.

incidents-bot: Alert: 5xx rate on /v1/generate decreased from 8.2% -> 0.15% within 5m after rollback.

maya: confirmed: errors dropped back to baseline by 09:50 UTC. Customer notified (samir handled messaging).

samir: customer update: "Thanks — errors cleared and we're back to normal. We'll reopen if we see anything else."

ryan: logging for postmortem: root cause = enabling trace header without size caps + canary gating not catching production-scale header lengths. Impact: short outage (09:38-09:49), ~intermittent 502/504 for 10% of traffic.

leo: next steps (short):
- Add test that simulates large trace sizes and verifies proxy behavior (jordan)
- Add runtime guard to not send header if >2KB and log metric for dropped-trace-header (jordan)
- Add canary healthcheck to detect gateway 502/5xx spikes with stricter abort (platform)
- Update runbook: include header-size risk in rollout checklist (maya/ryan)

jordan: also will add a prometheus metric trace_header_size_bytes and an alert when 95th > 1600 bytes.

maya: can we include a quick config change to increase proxy buffer for now? I prefer not — better to limit header emission.

leo: agreed. Do we want a formal postmortem? Seems short but could affect customers.

ryan: yes, schedule a follow-up postmortem doc, assign owner jordan, draft due EOD tomorrow.

maya: thanks everyone. closing thread once postmortem created. :white_check_mark:
